what_happened: A flaw nicknamed ClawJacked in a popular open-source AI agent let an ordinary website take over the agent running on someone's own machine. The page opened a connection to the agent's local port, guessed its password, and then gave the agent orders. The researchers who found it reported it, and a fix shipped within a day.
lesson: Local-only does not mean safe. Anything you run on localhost can be reached by a browser tab, so a local agent needs a real password, a limit on guesses, and a check on who is calling.

evidence.claim: A malicious website could connect to the agent's gateway on localhost over a WebSocket and brute-force its password
The vendor fixed it within about 24 hours of the report
The fix is in version 2026.2.25 or later
